sentences: A man in the kitchen is quite an uncommon sight.

issues: The sentence is a copular predication with an indefinite subject, which the instruction set routes to the generic kind form (Inheritance on the kind, as in "A dog is a mammal"), but the parse mints a specific witness sk_man_1 and predicates by Member.
(LocatedIn sk_man_1 sk_kitchen_1) asserts that a particular man is actually in a particular kitchen — an existential and locative commitment the generic sentence never makes.

"uncommon" is the kind-level, non-distributing family the instruction set names explicitly (common / rare / widespread / numerous), so it should route to KindProperty rather than Member on an individual — one man cannot be uncommon.
(Member sk_man_1 sight) predicates sight-hood of the man himself, whereas the sentence says the scene of a man being in a kitchen is the uncommon sight.

The consequent's negation ('could not live') is dropped entirely, so the sealed bundle records the positive 'people could live for ten minutes', the opposite of what the sentence says.
The live event's subject takes `Experiencer`, while the instruction set's own example ('Mia has lived in Oslo since 2019') assigns `Agent` to a live subject.

`ten_minutes` is an invented constant with no class atom (an untyped referent symbol), and the tag attaches to `sk_live_1`, an event that exists only inside the seal.

resolution.note: genus chain asserts friends literally thieves; Possession misapplied

issues: `Possession` is misapplied: the genitive rule explicitly excludes an "about"/object of-phrase, and "thieves OF time" is the notional object of the nominalization, not a possessor — as written the atom says time possesses the thief.

Fusing the N + of-PP "thieves of time" into the compound symbol `thief_of_time` is not one of the licensed compound shapes (compound action, phrasal verb, modifier_noun / adjective+noun kind, possessive NP).
The definitional genus at 1.0/0.99 combined with statement 0 derives that friends are literally thieves, asserting the figurative predication as fact.

sentences: Education has nothing to do with age.
statements: (: edu_age_ntdw (And (Member sk_htdw_1 have_to_do_with) (Holder sk_htdw_1 education) (Theme sk_htdw_1 age)) (STV 0.0 0.99))

resolution.note: mild: kind-relation form-branch miss + Holder misread + TV over-commit

issues: Both arguments are bare kind-denoting mass NPs ("education", "age"), which is exactly the stated trigger for the kind-level relational generic `(<Verb> <kindA> <kindB>)`; reifying an event with roles instead is the drift between the two incomparable forms the instructions warn against.

`Holder` is reserved for a possession/relational state (own/have/lack); the surface "has" here is part of the idiom `have_to_do_with` and asserts no possession, so the role is read off the surface verb rather than the idiom's meaning.
Confidence 0.99 treats an empirical, contingent generalization as an individual fact; the definitional-vs-empirical dial calls for 0.9.

sentences: The freedom movement started as a trickle and turned into a gusher.

resolution.note: false tenseless 'is a trickle'; sibling parse proves licensed route existed

issues: The "as a trickle" phase-state is emitted as a flat, tenseless (Member sk_freedom_movement_1 trickle), so the KB asserts the movement simply is a trickle — unbounded in time, un-linked to the start event, and missing the Past wrapper a past copular state takes.
"turned into a gusher" is a change of kind, not motion, so the spatial Goal oblique (reserved for "into / onto / to" paths) misreads the construction.
A separate witness sk_gusher_1 is minted for what the sentence says the movement itself became, so nothing in the parse records the identity of the movement with the gusher.

sentences: Hit men are a popular subject for TV movies.

issues: popular_subject_for_tv_movies fuses an adjective, a head noun and a whole PP complement into one symbol, which the compound rules do not license — compounds are two-word modifier_noun / verb_object / verb_particle, decomposed once into single-word lemmas.

By the stated KindProperty test (could one individual hold it?) an individual hit man could be a popular subject for TV movies, so the bare-plural copular generic should be ordinary Inheritance, not the non-distributing KindProperty reserved for extinct / widespread / common.
"TV movies" never surfaces as a referable kind (no tv_movie symbol, no (Inheritance tv_movie movie)), so nothing in the KB can answer what hit men are a popular subject for.

Exposing the modifier genus (Inheritance popular_subject_for_tv_movies popular) presupposes a licensed fusion, but "popular subject" is incidental description, which the adjective+noun rule says never to fuse.

sentences: Come on now, please stand up, Mr. Rothschild.

resolution.note: over-strict; gap valid (exhortation/'please')

issues: The first imperative clause 'Come on now' yields no atoms at all — no second `Directive` over a `come_on` eventuality, and nothing for 'now' or 'please'.

sentences: To Laura. Happy 40th birthday. Love, Pete.

resolution.note: corpus-defect flavored (greeting-card fragments past filter) but parse unrecoverable; wish asserted as fact

issues: The well-wish is asserted as fact: (Member sk_birthday_1 happy) at strength 1.0 claims the birthday IS happy, which the text never states.

The dedication "To Laura" and the sign-off "Love, Pete" are unrepresented — laura and pete are bare Name atoms with no relation to the birthday or to each other, and the birthday is never tied to Laura.

sentences: The mental world is usually considered to be subjective and not objective .

resolution.note: epistemic flattening: 'is considered to be' dropped, opinion asserted as fact

issues: The reporting frame "is usually considered to be" is dropped entirely and the property is asserted of the kind outright, so the parse states as fact what the text only reports as a general opinion — a violation of "assert only what the text states".
Same flattening on the negated conjunct: "not objective" is asserted at strength 0.0 at top level rather than under the dropped "considered" frame.

sentences: There is only one book on the desk.

resolution.note: 'only' dropped + no individual typed: existential QA cannot bind

issues: The exclusive focus particle "only" is dropped entirely — no (Only ...) atom, so "only one book" and "one book" produce identical parses.

The singular "one book" is encoded as a group with Cardinality 1 rather than the existential witness the singular licenses, so no individual is ever typed (Member sk_book_1 book) and "is there a book on the desk?" cannot bind.

sentences: A woman is the sweetest thing in the world.

issues: The restrictor "in the world" is dropped entirely — no atom records the domain over which the superlative ranks.
(Inheritance woman thing) is taxonomic (no counterexample conceivable), so the confidence dial calls for 0.99, not the empirical 0.9.

sentences: Language is one of the most systematic, subtle, and significant vehicles for spreading racist ideology.

resolution.note: unasserted spread event at 1.0 + superlative-partitive flattened + Degree-slot abuse

issues: "one of the most ... vehicles" is flattened to a plain generic (Inheritance language vehicle): the "one of the" partitive over a definite superset and the superlative ranking are both lost.

(Degree language systematic most) uses the superlative word as a Degree level, but the level slot is restricted to a lemmatized surface intensifier adverb or the three construction markers excessive/sufficient/insufficient, and superlatives route to (Most <scale> X <class>) instead.
Same unlicensed "most" level on (Degree language subtle most).
Same unlicensed "most" level on (Degree language significant most).

A spreading event is asserted at top level at (STV 1.0 0.99), but the sentence only says the vehicles are *for* spreading — no spreading is claimed to occur, so this asserts more than the text states.
(Instrument sk_spread_1 language) attaches a role to that unasserted event, and nothing anywhere records the "for"-relation between the vehicle claim and the spreading.

The three adjectives are attributive on "vehicles" inside the superlative NP, yet are predicated of language directly at generic strength, so the ranking-among-vehicles reading is replaced by three plain generics.

sentences: This shirt is also available in green.

resolution.note: false content: 'this shirt is green' asserted; Also mis-slotted

issues: (Member sk_shirt_1 green) asserts that this shirt IS green, but the text says only that a green version is available, so the atom over-asserts a property the words do not put there.

(Also green sk_shirt_1) puts an entity witness in the slot the instruction set reserves for the event — the copular clause reifies no event, so the focus atom's second argument has no licensed filler.

sentences: There was a massive amount of blood all over the floor.

resolution.note: graceful improvisation in gap territory; atoms true

issues: The `quantity` scale of `Degree` is defined only for the too-much / too-little / enough construction with the three fixed markers excessive / insufficient / sufficient, so the level symbol `massive` is outside the licensed set for that slot.

sentences: Every molecule of water is composed of two hydrogen atoms attached to an oxygen atom.
statements: (: molecule_composed (Implication (Member $x water_molecule) (And (Member (sk_compose $x) compose) (Patient (sk_compose $x) $x) (Agent (sk_compose $x) (sk_h $x)) (GroupOf (sk_h $x) hydrogen_atom) (Cardinality (sk_h $x) 2) (Member (sk_attach $x) attach) (Patient (sk_attach $x) (sk_h $x)) (Goal (sk_attach $x) (sk_o $x)) (Member (sk_o $x) oxygen_atom))) (STV 1.0 0.99))

resolution.note: mild: Patient for stative constitution (default Theme); consistency w/ tierC-000161

issues: (Patient (sk_compose $x) $x) gives the molecule the Patient role, but "is composed of" is a stative constitution predicate that creates, destroys, consumes or physically changes nothing, so the object test — and its "when unclear, default to Theme" fallback — yields Theme.

sentences: David Ross was the announcer and Carl Fenton conducted the orchestra .

resolution.note: one mandated enrichment atom missing; nothing false

issues: `announcer` passes both agent-nominalization tests and is the copular predicate of its clause, so the rule ('where it fires is fixed, not a judgment call') requires (Inheritance announcer (can announce)), which the parse does not emit.

sentences: A wart is a generally benign and slightly contagious infection.

issues: Strength 1.0 for (Inheritance wart benign) drops the "generally" hedge entirely and is stronger than the 0.9 the instruction set assigns even an unhedged bare generic, so a hedged claim comes out asserted at full strength.
(Inheritance wart contagious) is a bare generic property of a kind, which the quantity-to-strength rule puts at strength 0.9 (≈most), not 1.0.

sentences: Most writers are sensitive to criticism.

resolution.note: mild: severed uninterpretable (To writer criticism) at 1.0/0.99

issues: The adjective's PP complement is emitted as a free-standing kind-to-kind atom (To writer criticism), severing "to criticism" from the sensitive property so nothing records that the sensitivity is TO criticism.
That atom is asserted at (STV 1.0 0.99) although the sentence quantifies only "most" writers, over-committing relative to the 0.9 strength carried by the Inheritance atom it is meant to modify.

sentences: The gamma function is a generalization of the factorial function.

resolution.note: borderline; possessive paraphrase valid here; nominalization-of gap is the product

issues: The of-complement of the nominalization "a generalization of the factorial function" is encoded as (Possession sk_gamma_function_1 sk_factorial_function_1), which the genitive rule's own exclusion list argues against (it is neither ownership/kinship nor part-whole but the argument of a nominalization) and which, read possessed-first, asserts that the gamma function belongs to the factorial function.

Because the of-phrase is detached from the generalization atom, the sentence's actual content — that the gamma function generalizes the factorial function — is recoverable only by stitching statements 4 and 5 together.

sentences: The Durga puja is performed in homes and public.

issues: The elliptical second conjunct "(in) public" is a circumstantial adverbial meaning "publicly / in the open", not a place, so (Location sk_perform_1 public) asserts a spatial filler named public that the phrase does not name — the PP does not really answer "where".

sentences: The fountain is full of women.

resolution.note: entailed content; adjective+of-complement gap is the product

issues: The of-complement of the adjective 'full' is rendered as a spatial containment claim (LocatedIn group-in-fountain) that no locative word in the sentence licenses.
'full' is emitted as a bare one-place property of the fountain, so nothing ties the fullness to the women and the of-phrase's contribution is unrecoverable from the two atoms taken together.

sentences: Corruption was widespread in Persia , and discipline in the army was dangerously lax .

resolution.note: restriction stripped: widespread-at-large over-assertion; kinds in entity slots

issues: The KindProperty claim is left unrestricted — the text says corruption was widespread *in Persia*, not widespread at large, and the restriction is stripped off the property atom.

(LocatedIn corruption persia) puts a bare kind/mass symbol in a head specified for 'where a THING is' (an entity), and it is asserted untensed while the property it is meant to restrict is Past-wrapped.
(Inheritance discipline lax) asserts laxness of discipline in general, whereas the subject is the specific 'discipline in the army'.
(LocatedIn discipline sk_army_1) again places a kind in the entity slot and treats an army (an organization) as a containing place.

sentences: There are some brown balls in the red basket.

issues: "brown" is a descriptive (colour) modifier on a plural, which the instruction set says distributes over the members via the per-member rule ranging over (PartOf $x sk_group_1); (Member sk_group_1 brown) instead predicates brown of the group-as-object, the reading the Quantifiers section explicitly warns against.

sentences: Thanks for agreeing to come.

resolution.note: corpus-defect flavored ellipsis; sealed roleless complement loses who-comes; owner flags doctrine Q: implicit speaker/addressee for expressives

issues: The complement of 'agree' is sealed as a term argument, but sealing is licensed only for finite clausal attitude complements, embedded questions, imperatives, counterfactuals and strength-0 denials — a matrix verb with a non-finite complement reifies that eventuality at top level under Theme instead.
The sealed complement carries only its event class, with no Agent or any other role, so nothing in the parse records who was to come.

sentences: The film is a first Syrian nominated film produced and directed for Oscar .

issues: The pre-nominal participle "nominated" in "a first Syrian nominated film" is reified as a nominate event (statements 5-7), but the instruction set treats a participle used as a modifier before its noun as an adjective ("a laminated worktop" -> (Member sk_worktop_1 laminated)) and reserves the reduced-relative event form for participial POST-modifiers such as "produced and directed".

sentences: The milk is sold in glass bottles.

issues: The definite 'the milk' is filled by the bare class symbol milk with no typing atom, but the instruction set reserves bare class symbols for non-specific/generic objects and requires a definite description to mint a typed individual (sk_milk_1 plus its Member atom).

Location places the selling event inside the glass bottles, whereas 'in glass bottles' names the container the milk is sold in rather than where the selling happened, so the where-question test for the named role fails.

sentences: The speeder was pulled over and fined.

issues: 'pulled over' assigns Patient although being pulled over neither creates, destroys, consumes nor changes the speeder — it is forced displacement, which the instruction set explicitly keeps on Theme, as the coordinate 'fined' conjunct itself does for the same participant.

sentences: The final was postponed until tomorrow.

issues: (End sk_postpone_1 tomorrow) puts a future endpoint on an event already marked Past, and 'until tomorrow' names the final's new scheduled time rather than the extent of the postponing act.

sentences: The performance was low-keyed.

issues: The predicate adjective 'low-keyed' is rendered as the derived base low_key, but the inflection-only rule keeps an adjectival/participial surface form as it stands (low_keyed), leaving synonym collapse to downstream normalization.

sentences: As an official Soviet artist , his work was well received and exhibited widely .

issues: "Soviet artist" is left as two independent properties (statements 1 and 3) instead of the fused compound kind the instruction set directs for a nationality/origin adjective plus noun (breton_tapestry), which would be (Member sk_person_1 soviet_artist) plus (Inheritance soviet_artist artist) and (Inheritance soviet_artist soviet).

sentences: Love is a game in which one always cheats.

issues: The relative clause "in which one always cheats" becomes an unrestricted rule over every person, asserting that everyone cheats rather than that cheating happens in this game.
"always" is dropped — no frequency or universal-occurrence marker records it anywhere in the parse.

(Location (sk_cheat $x) game) uses the bare class symbol game for the specific game the relative pronoun "which" picks out (love itself), which the instruction set reserves for non-specific/generic objects, and treats an abstract game as a spatial container.

sentences: That could take a while.

issues: "a while" — a vague duration — is encoded as an entity of a coined class while, positing an object the sentence never introduces and losing the duration meaning entirely.
Making that while-entity the Theme unpacks the non-literal "take a while" into a literal taking event, which the idiom coherence test rules out (nothing is grasped or transferred).

sentences: The game was put off till next week.

issues: "till next week" is attached as (Time sk_put_off_1 next_week), asserting that the putting-off itself happened next week — which contradicts the (Past sk_put_off_1) on the same event; "till/until Y" is the interval End form, and here it names the game's new schedule, not the time of the postponing.

sentences: Different rules may apply to non-citizens.

issues: The verbal event-rule form is used for a MODAL generic, which the instruction set restricts to non-modal generics ('Only a non-modal verbal generic ("birds fly") takes the event rule').

Putting (Might (sk_apply $x)) inside the consequent converts the sentence's proposition-level possibility ('it may be that different rules apply to non-citizens') into a per-instance claim ('any different rule might apply').

sentences: The movie is a harrowing depiction of life in an urban slum.

issues: (LocatedIn sk_life_1 sk_slum_1) applies the entity-position head to an abstract noun, where the instruction set defines LocatedIn for where a THING is (a village in a county, a jetty in an estuary).

sentences: This is no way to treat a lady.

issues: The treating event is asserted at top level at (STV 1.0 0.99), but the sentence asserts no treating occurrence — 'a way to treat a lady' is an infinitival relative describing a manner, not a reported event.
sk_lady_1 posits a specific lady as an existing individual, where 'a lady' inside the infinitival relative is generic (any lady) and no lady is introduced by the sentence.

(Manner sk_treat_1 sk_thing_1) uses Manner with an entity filler, where the instruction set defines Manner as taking a surface adverb; it also reverses the dependency (the infinitive modifies 'way', it is not an adjunct of a treating event).

The strength-0 atom denies the literal predication 'this is a way', whereas the sentence denies acceptability ('this is not an acceptable way') — combined with the positive Manner link at statement 5 the parse both denies and asserts that this is how the lady is treated.

sentences: Nobody will likely even notice.

issues: The scalar focus tag (Even notice (sk_notice $x)) sits inside the strength-0.0 consequent, so the focus record is itself denied rather than recorded, contrary to the Yet precedent that a presupposition tag stays outside the strength-0 denial.

The epistemic (Probably (sk_notice $x)) is likewise inside the denied bundle, yielding the narrow 'for each person, not probably-notice' scope rather than the natural 'it is likely that nobody notices'.

sentences: Oh, that kid went to sleep without eating supper.
statements: (: eat_neg (And (Member sk_eat_1 eat) (Agent sk_eat_1 sk_kid_1) (Patient sk_eat_1 supper) (Past sk_eat_1)) (STV 0.0 0.99))

issues: 'went to sleep' is decomposed into a literal motion event (Member sk_go_1 go) with (Goal sk_go_1 sleep), but sleep is not a destination so the literal reading is incoherent for these participants, and the idiom coherence test then calls for one surface symbol keeping every word.

sentences: Tickets will go on sale next Tuesday.

issues: The bare plural 'Tickets' is given a group witness, which the determiner rule reserves for definite / demonstrative / possessed plurals — a bare plural is routed to the generic kind — so the quantificational route taken is not the one the instruction set specifies.
Having taken the group route with a distributive predicate, the parse emits no per-member (PartOf $x sk_group_1) distribution rule alongside the group event, which the grouped-plural rule requires.

sentences: There was no service. Not even a bar.

issues: The scalar focus particle 'even' is dropped entirely — no (Even ...) atom is emitted — so the second sentence's only content beyond a bare denial is lost.
The quantifier 'no' gets no QuantifierPhrase companion, which Negation (copular) requires of 'no' / 'none' precisely so a quantifier-none reading stays distinct from a plain 'not' denial.

sentences: It was believed by this method true philosophy could be separated from popular wisdom .
statements: (: e_theme (Theme sk_believe_1 (And (Member sk_separate_1 separate) (Patient sk_separate_1 true_philosophy) (Source sk_separate_1 popular_wisdom) (Can sk_separate_1))) (STV 1.0 0.99))

issues: 'by this method' names the means of the separating, not of the believing (a method cannot be the passive by-phrase agent of 'believed'), so the Instrument atom is misattached to sk_believe_1 and asserted at top level instead of sitting inside the sealed complement on sk_separate_1.

'separated from' leaves true philosophy distinguished rather than altered, and the role test is at best unclear here, so the instruction set's 'when the test is unclear, default to Theme' rule makes the sealed (Patient sk_separate_1 true_philosophy) the wrong role.

sentences: A deck of cards contains four kings, four queens, and four jacks.

issues: The coordinated object 'four kings, four queens, and four jacks' is packed as three Theme atoms on one contain event, whereas coordinated noun phrases are distributive by default (replicate the predication once per conjunct); one event carrying several same-role atoms is licensed only as the collective multiple-Agent form.

sentences: This is the something many people seem to overlook.

issues: The matrix equative clause "This is the something ..." is entirely unparsed - no witness or atom for the subject "This" and no atom identifying it with the overlooked thing, so the sentence's main predication is missing.

The referent is typed with the pronoun itself, (Member sk_something_1 something), rather than a real kind such as thing, against the rule that a bare pronoun's witness is minted from its class and never from the pronoun.

sentences: Translating sentences is not an easy task.

issues: (Member sk_translate_1 task) is asserted at strength 1.0 even though the text says only that translating is *not* an easy task; the denial is applied to `easy` alone, so the parse positively asserts half of the very predicate nominal the sentence negates.
The gerundive subject "Translating sentences" is reified as an ordinary positive event witness, asserting that a translating eventuality holds rather than predicating of the activity itself.

sentences: Edmundo sat right behind Melissa in class.

issues: "right behind Melissa" answers *where*, which the oblique rule routes to the named role Location; the preposition-named (Behind ...) form is licensed only when no named role fits, and the instruction set says to decide by the question the PP answers.

sentences: The Moroccan police cracked down on the protests.

issues: The event class absorbs the governing preposition into the verb symbol (crack_down_on) where the instruction set's phrasal-verb form is verb + particle only (crack_down), so this class will not unify with the same verb recorded elsewhere.

The object of "on" is given the direct-object role Patient instead of the preposition-named oblique (On <event> sk_protest_1) that the instruction set prescribes for a PP naming what the activity is directed at ("depend **on** the pump", "work **on** the mural").

sentences: The thermometer reads three degrees below zero.

issues: The reading is attributed to the thermometer as its own temperature and the "reads" clause is dropped entirely, whereas the sentence asserts what the instrument displays; the instruction set's stative-transitive rule ("the manifest lists two pallets", "the tank holds forty litres" -> Agent) would instead reify a read event with the thermometer as Agent.

sentences: No one likes being yelled at.

issues: The yelling event's atoms sit as bare conjuncts of the strength-0.0 consequent rather than sealed as a term, so the denial scopes over the yelling too — the rule reads "for each person, NOT (x likes E AND E is a yelling at x)", which is satisfied by nobody ever being yelled at, losing the distinction between "no one likes it" and "no one is yelled at".

sentences: The students are happy, but the teachers are not.

issues: Neither copular connective endpoint emits the flat copular atom the dual-emit rule requires — no `(Member sk_group_1 happy)` beside the reified `sk_happy_1` state, and no strength-0 flat twin for the teachers.

sentences: The PacifiCats were designed by Philip Hercus from Vancouver and Robert Allan Limited of Australia .

issues: "The PacifiCats" is a capitalized proper name (a named vessel class) but is silently converted into the common kind `pacificat` with no `(Name ...)` atom at all, against the rule that every proper noun — vessels included — carries exactly one Name fact.

"Robert Allan Limited of Australia" is an entity-attached genitive, yet it is rendered as the positional claim `(LocatedIn robert_allan_limited australia)` instead of the ordinary genitive `Possession`, asserting a position the text never states — while the sister phrase "Philip Hercus from Vancouver" is correctly kept as the surface `From`.

sentences: Henry Cole was followed by Bailey as Caretaker of Breakheart Hill .

issues: The determiner-less role nominal "Caretaker" is given a witness individual `sk_caretaker_1` instead of the bare class constant the oblique-object rule prescribes for an article-less nominal, so the parse posits a separate caretaker entity that is never linked to Bailey.

sentences: Gabor was stuck in that place.

issues: The copular predicate-adjective state is reified as a state witness although none of the enumerated reification triggers is present (resultative, connective-atom endpoint, or a time modifier) — the instruction set says to reify only then and otherwise emit just the flat copular atom.

The locative "in that place" is attached as an event-oblique `Location` on that invented state witness, where the instruction set routes where a THING is onto the static `(LocatedIn <entity> <place>)`.

sentences: These predictive functions , in a non-spatial context are referred to as pedotransfer functions .

issues: The demonstrative plural is recorded only as a group-level event; no per-member distribution rule over `(PartOf $x sk_function_1)` accompanies it, although being referred to as a pedotransfer function holds of each function separately and the grouped-plural rule pairs the group event with the per-member rule.

sentences: There was nothing to be seen but fog.

issues: The clause's negative existential ("there was nothing ...") is dropped entirely — no strength-0 atom appears anywhere; the negation is re-expressed as the positive focus atom (Only fog sk_see_1), a form the instruction set licenses only for "only / just / solely".
(Can sk_see_1) reads a capability off the infinitival "to be seen" although the clause carries none of the "can / able to" markers the status-predicate rule requires.

sentences: The zoo in Prague is not so big.

issues: The degree hedge "so" is dropped entirely, so the parse states the flat denial "the zoo is not big" rather than the weaker hedged claim "not so big" (≈ not particularly big).

sentences: No one received enough votes to win the nomination.
statements: (: no_one_rule (Implication (Member $x person) (And (Member (sk_receive $x) receive) (Agent (sk_receive $x) $x) (Theme (sk_receive $x) (sk_votes $x)) (GroupOf (sk_votes $x) vote) (Degree (sk_votes $x) quantity sufficient) (Past (sk_receive $x)) (Member (sk_win $x) win) (Agent (sk_win $x) $x) (Theme (sk_win $x) sk_nomination_1))) (STV 0.0 0.9))

issues: The 'enough ... to V' consequence (the winning) carries no operator, but the instruction set requires the enabled action of a sufficient-quantity/degree construction to be emitted with (Can e) or (Permitted e) picked by sense (ability vs eligibility), as in 'Sam is fit enough to run'.

Folding the win atoms into the same strength-0 conjunction as the receiving makes the claim a conjunction denial ('no person both received sufficient votes and won the nomination') rather than a denial that anyone's votes were sufficient for winning, which is a weaker and different claim.

sentences: The Pustnic River or Orociu River is a tributary of the River Oraciu in Romania .

issues: Two `Name` atoms are hung on one symbol ("Pustnic River" and "Orociu River"), against the rule that a proper noun gets exactly one Name fact — the alias "or" has no licensed encoding, so the alternative name is recorded in a form the instruction set forbids.

sentences: Milk is better than water.

issues: This is a contingent generalization about two kinds, so the definitional/empirical dial makes it (STV 1.0 0.9), not the individual-fact default (STV 1.0 0.99).

sentences: Regularly clean and maintain the exterior of the cabinets.
statements: (: clean_dir (Directive (And (Member sk_clean_1 clean) (Patient sk_clean_1 sk_exterior_1) (Manner sk_clean_1 regularly))) (STV 1.0 0.99))
(: maintain_dir (Directive (And (Member sk_maintain_1 maintain) (Patient sk_maintain_1 sk_exterior_1) (Manner sk_maintain_1 regularly))) (STV 1.0 0.99))

issues: 'maintain' takes Patient, but maintaining need not create/destroy/consume or physically change the exterior, and the instruction set says to default to Theme when the change test is unclear.

sentences: Hubble is in excellent health.

issues: The copular predicate 'is in excellent health' is rendered as a reified state witness with no licensing trigger — the instruction set reifies a copular state only for a time modifier or a connective endpoint, and then always dual-emits the flat copular atom, which is absent here, and the surface preposition 'in' is left unrepresented by any oblique.

sentences: The clock struck twelve at midnight.

issues: The direct object 'twelve' is re-encoded as a clock-hour Time atom, which under the mandated 24-hour convention asserts the striking happened at noon and so contradicts the sentence's own 'at midnight' adjunct; the object is simultaneously left with no participant role.

sentences: Cancer kills thousands of people every year.

issues: The bare kind 'cancer' is used as a constant Agent filler of a single unmarked event, but the instruction set licenses the bare class symbol only for a non-specific/generic OBJECT and routes a bare-kind subject with a habitual present predicate into the verbal-generic Implication rule form.

sentences: The Banach - Mackey - topology and the weak Arens - space topology are used relatively rarely .

issues: No (Name ...) atom is emitted for the eponymous named entity, and the lowercase common noun is folded into the name symbol, where the 'the Brindle estuary' rule prescribes (Member banach_mackey topology) plus (Name banach_mackey "Banach-Mackey").
Same omission for 'the weak Arens - space topology': no Name atom, and the capitalized 'Arens' is buried inside the fused compound symbol.

Both definite singular referents are encoded as kinds (Inheritance ... topology) and then used as bare class-symbol role fillers, while the definite-description rule prescribes a typed individual and reserves bare class symbols for non-specific objects.
'relatively' is silently dropped from 'relatively rarely', and the frequency adverb 'rarely' is filed under Manner.

sentences: She and her sisters also performed in cafes and sang music to accompany silent films .

issues: The sisters group gets group-level perform/sing events but no per-member distribution rule over (PartOf $x sk_group_1), which the instruction set requires for a grouped plural with a distributive predicate (the 'the dogs barked' case).

sentences: The union bosses are fighting the freeze on wage hikes.

issues: The PP complement of the event-noun 'the freeze on wage hikes' is rendered as a thematic role (Patient sk_freeze_1 wage_hike), but thematic roles are defined only for reified event witnesses read off a clause, and the instruction set's guidance for a preposition attached to an entity is to keep the surface preposition, i.e. (On sk_freeze_1 wage_hike).

sentences: Attack is the best defense.

issues: (Inheritance attack defense) is a kind-level generalization for which a counterexample is plainly conceivable, so the definitional-vs-empirical dial calls for confidence 0.9, not the 0.99 emitted.

sentences: Giant posters of Saddam Hussein adorned public places.

issues: "giant" is an incidental-description (size) modifier on a plural, which the Compound-concepts rule says must distribute over the group's members like a copular predicate (a rule over (PartOf $x sk_poster_1)), not be predicated of the group symbol itself as (Member sk_poster_1 giant).

sentences: There was a different kind of atmosphere in the headquarters.

issues: Past is wrapped only around the LocatedIn atom while the clause's other categorical atoms (Member sk_atmosphere_1 atmosphere / different) are left unwrapped, whereas the tense rule states the past wrapper applies to every categorical atom the clause yields — the parse is internally inconsistent about whether this clause is tensed.
"a different kind of atmosphere" is flattened to an atmosphere that is different, dropping the kind-level layer of "kind of" and the implicit standard "different" is measured against.

sentences: That phone number never existed.
statements: (: pn_not_exist (And (Member sk_exist_1 exist) (Experiencer sk_exist_1 sk_phone_number_1) (Past sk_exist_1)) (STV 0.0 0.99))

issues: the top-level (Member sk_phone_number_1 phone_number) asserts at strength 1.0 that such a number exists, which is exactly what the sentence denies; the definite/demonstrative projection rule licenses the atom, so this looks like a rule gap rather than a parser slip.

sentences: Russia is not the victim in its war on Ukraine.

issues: The restrictive PP 'in its war on Ukraine' is never linked to the victim denial, so the parse denies Russia's victimhood unrestrictedly instead of only within that war.

sentences: These Tuareg had large herds of cows.

issues: Plural 'herds' is collapsed into a single herd witness, so the sentence's multiple herds - and the distribution of 'large' over them - are lost.
The demonstrative plural subject gets a group-only possession event with no per-member distribution rule, which the instruction set reserves for collective predicates (gather/meet/assemble).

sentences: This is the end of the road.

issues: The demonstrative subject "This" gets no symbol and no class atom, although the instruction set makes a witness plus its class atom mandatory for a pronoun with no antecedent (it -> the salient kind, else thing).
The clause's predication is unrepresented: the three atoms assert only the presupposed existence of a road and its end, so nothing in the parse records the claim the sentence actually makes.

sentences: Europe looks like a paradise now.

issues: Typing the reified state witness with the NOMINAL complement asserts an unhedged paradise instance at (STV 1.0 0.99) — the epistemic hedge sits only on the separate Probably atoms, so "is there a paradise?" binds at full strength even though the sentence only says Europe looks like one.

sentences: Be careful not to bump the stereo when moving things around.
statements: (: e_bump_forbid (Forbid (And (Member sk_bump_1 bump) (Theme sk_bump_1 sk_stereo_1) (Member sk_move_1 move_around) (Theme sk_move_1 thing) (Ongoing sk_move_1) (During sk_bump_1 sk_move_1))) (STV 1.0 0.99))

issues: "Be careful" is sealed as a bare state witness sk_careful_1 carrying no Experiencer or other participant, and nothing links that directive to the bumping it cautions against, so one instruction is recorded as two unrelated commands.

(Ongoing sk_move_1) is asserted for the participial temporal adjunct "when moving things around", which is none of the exactly four markers the instruction set allows for Ongoing (there is no progressive auxiliary, inceptive, continuative perfect or perception complement).

sentences: Celestia invites Twilight and her friends to stop the elements of harmony to recover Chrysalis .

issues: The invitee ("Twilight and her friends") never appears on the invite event itself — only as Agent inside the embedded stop event — so the sentence's core relation "Celestia invites Twilight" is unrecoverable.
"stop the elements" is given Patient although stopping neither creates, destroys, consumes nor physically changes them, so the unclear-case default Theme applies (same at statement 22).

sentences: There can be but one victor.

issues: Can is defined as a specific subject's capability on an event, or as a status operator wrapping a categorical Member/Inheritance atom, but here it wraps a GroupOf typing atom and is being used for impersonal possibility ('there can be'), so the modal is attached to the wrong content.
The uniqueness claim (CardinalityAtMost sk_victor_1 1) is asserted flat, outside the modal, so the parse states as fact what the sentence only says is possible.
sk_victor_1 has no top-level typing atom — its only class atom (GroupOf) sits inside the Can wrapper, leaving an untyped referent symbol at top level.

sentences: The vampire transformed into a bat.

issues: The flat (Member sk_vampire_1 bat) asserts tenselessly that the vampire is a bat, but a flat result atom is licensed only as half of the resultative dual-emit, and neither half of the licensing structure is present — no reified result state with Experiencer, no (Result <event> <state>) link.

The resulting kind is encoded twice in incompatible ways: 'a bat' is already a separate witness sk_bat_1 attached by the Into oblique, so the extra flat atom predicates bat-hood of the vampire while a distinct bat individual also stands.

sentences: Methoni is a village and a former municipality in Pieria regional unit , Greece .

issues: "a former municipality" is wrapped in Past even though the copula is present tense (the instruction set makes the surface tense decide mechanically), and the "is not one now" half that "former" asserts is not recorded anywhere.

sentences: New Zealand was isolated for 80 million years.

issues: "was isolated for 80 million years" functions as a durative predicate-adjective state (no agent, stative for-duration), which the instruction set routes as a copular clause — a reified state with Experiencer plus the flat (Past (Member new_zealand isolated)) — whereas the parse reifies an agentless passive isolating event.

sentences: There used to be a big cherry tree in the garden.
statements: (: tree_denial (And (Member sk_tree_1 cherry_tree) (Member sk_tree_1 big) (LocatedIn sk_tree_1 sk_garden_1)) (STV 0.0 0.99))

issues: (Past sk_tree_1) puts a tense status atom directly on an entity witness, but status predicates take an event witness and tense over a copular/entity-level state must wrap the categorical atom instead ((Past (Member ...)) / (Past (LocatedIn ...))).

Because the Past never attaches to them, the tree's typing, size and location atoms stand asserted at strength 1.0 as present facts alongside their own strength-0 denial, so nothing marks the positive half as the past state the cessation pattern intends.

sentences: Things like that happen more often now.
statements: (: things_happen_rule (Implication (And (Member $x thing) (Like $x sk_thing_1)) (And (Member (sk_happen $x) happen) (Agent (sk_happen $x) $x) (Time (sk_happen $x) now) (Manner (sk_happen $x) more_often))) (STV 0.9 0.9))

issues: "more often" is a frequency comparative, but it is stuffed into (Manner (sk_happen $x) more_often) as an invented multi-word filler — the instruction set reserves Manner for a surface adverb, encodes comparison with More/MoreBy, and encodes frequency with Every/TimesPer, so the comparison is lost entirely.

"happen" with a non-volitional subject is given Agent, though the intransitive-subject test points at an undergoer role (the thing does not initiate the happening); the "when unclear, Agent" fallback is the only cover.

sentences: This is one of the greatest mysteries in all of science.

issues: The superlative "greatest" is flattened to the plain positive property great, dropping the superlative claim the sentence makes.
That property is attached by Member to the group witness, so it predicates greatness of the group as a single object instead of distributing to the mysteries in it.
"in all of science" loses the "all of" — only the bare domain constant survives in the framing oblique.

sentences: The sun emerged from behind the clouds.

issues: "from behind the clouds" is rendered as (Source sk_emerge_1 sk_clouds_1), which says the sun came out of the clouds themselves and drops the "behind" spatial relation entirely.

sentences: He also appeared in music films and later in life , in comedic roles .

issues: "in comedic roles" is not a place — the appearing did not happen at a location called comedic_role — so it answers "in what capacity", not "where", and takes the preposition-named oblique rather than Location.
"in music films" names the medium/work rather than a where-PP, so Location over-commits here too.
"also" sits on the predicate, so the focus filler should be the verb-class lemma (appear), not the subject witness; it is also tagged on only the first of the two coordinated appearing events.

sentences: The old adaptor stopped working suddenly.

issues: The subject of the aspectual stop event is given Patient, but the instruction set's own "When did the ferry stop running?" query pattern stores that subject as Agent (with Theme = the activity), so this statement will not match the question form the prompt prescribes.

sentences: The highest amount of points possible on reports is 10 points.

issues: The whole clause is compressed into a single MeasureAtMost atom: the superlative subject NP ("the highest amount of points") and the "possible" modality leave no trace, so nothing records that a maximum attainable value is being specified rather than an observed bound.

The scale slot repeats the unit (point as both scale and unit) instead of naming a surface dimension, so the measure carries no usable dimension label and will not match any dimension-scaled question.
The entity slot holds the bare kind report, a position the Measures section only ever fills with an individual or group witness; a Measure on a kind does not distribute to any actual report.

sentences: Pure dingoes, like wolves, are still locked genetically into annual breeding cycles.
statements: (: dingo_locked_rule (Implication (Member $x pure_dingo) (And (Member (sk_lock $x) locked) (Experiencer (sk_lock $x) $x) (Into (sk_lock $x) annual_breeding_cycle) (Manner (sk_lock $x) genetically) (Like (sk_lock $x) wolf) (Still (sk_lock $x)))) (STV 0.9 0.9))

issues: The clause is a bare-plural COPULAR generic ("are ... locked"), which the instruction set keeps as a single Inheritance fact — copular universals/generics explicitly do not reify events — yet the parse emits a distributing Implication rule over a reified state.

The reified state emits no flat copular counterpart (no Inheritance pure_dingo locked, and no (Member $x locked) in the conclusion), so the dual-emit requirement for a reified copular state is unmet and a plain "are pure dingoes locked?" cannot bind.

(Like (sk_lock $x) wolf) hangs the parenthetical similative on the locking event, but "like wolves" compares the SUBJECT (dingoes are like wolves in being so locked), so the atom asserts a similarity the sentence does not state.

sentences: The man was ashamed of being born poor.

issues: The copular state "was ashamed" is reified without the flat copular atom (Past (Member sk_man_1 ashamed)) — the instruction set allows either the flat form alone or reified-plus-flat, never reified alone, so "was the man ashamed?" cannot bind.

sentences: Either one is fine, but the former is more concise.

issues: The explicit adversative connective "but" is dropped: no surface-headed (But <clause1> <clause2>) atom is emitted, and neither clause's state is reified as a connective endpoint, so the stated relation between the two clauses is lost (no defeasible-exception construction consumes it here).

sentences: Ethel spent decades programming mainframes.

issues: The matrix verb 'spent' is not reified at all and its duration argument is folded onto the gerund event instead, whereas 'Two kinds of clause' reifies every verbal predicate and the light-verb exemption is written only for occurred / happened / took place over an event-noun.

sentences: This would be a terrible tragedy.

issues: 'would' is rendered as the epistemic operator Probably (statement 1 too), but the epistemic route is written for might / probably / must only, and the instruction set's single 'would' precedent ('it would rain') maps it to Future.

The subject 'This' has no antecedent, so it needs its own witness typing atom at top level, but the referent is typed only as 'tragedy' inside the modal wrapper, leaving the symbol untyped in everything the sentence actually asserts.

sentences: Fifty years ago anyone could have bought the land.

issues: Free-choice 'anyone' is encoded as a single anonymous person witness, i.e. an existential — the parse says some person could have bought the land, not that any/every person could, so the universal loses its force and the distributing Implication over (Member $x person) is what the quantifier section calls for.

sentences: Such a thing is of no account.

issues: 'Such a thing is ...' is an indefinite copular predication, which the categorical section reads as generic — an Inheritance on the kind at the empirical 0.9 / 0.9 — rather than a specific witness predicated by Member at 1.0 / 0.99.

The sentence's explicit 'no' is absorbed whole into the idiom symbol and the atom is asserted at strength 1.0, so no atom in the output carries the negation that the copular-negation rule attaches to an explicit not / no.

sentences: The climactic battle of the Mahabharata takes place on the battlefield of Kurukshetra.

issues: 'the climactic battle of the Mahabharata' is mapped to Possession, but the genitive section decides by ONE test — is the possessed a part / component of the possessor — and the climactic battle is an episode of the epic, which selects PartOf.

sentences: The strawberries are still fresh.

issues: The property is emitted only inside the aspectual tag - (Still (Member $x fresh)) - so the freshness itself is never asserted, whereas the instruction set asserts the eventuality normally and adds the opaque tag as a separate atom (cf. 'The server crashed again').
The tag is specified as a unary marker on an event witness, (Still <event>), but here it takes a categorical proposition as its argument, a form the instruction set never shows.

sentences: Fishing trawlers have fished out all the local waters.

issues: The explicit universal "all the local waters" is dropped: the object is filled by the group symbol sk_waters_1 as a single collective Patient, whereas an explicit "all the" universal must distribute as a per-member range — a second premise (PartOf $w sk_waters_1) with the Skolem event a function of both bindings — instead of a group-as-unit filler.
The mandatory QuantifierPhrase companion for the surface word "all" is missing (one companion per explicit quantifier phrase, emitted whenever the word is actually there).

sentences: The children need to go to bed immediately.

issues: 'immediately' is recorded as Manner, but it answers 'when' rather than 'how', and the instruction set assigns adjunct roles by the question the adjunct answers (the same choice is repeated inside the rule at statement 6).

sentences: Fyodor sat there wide awake for about five hours.

issues: The depictive 'wide awake' is asserted as a bare unmarked atom under a Past host clause, so it claims Fyodor is awake now, whereas the instruction set has a clause's categorical atoms take the host clause's tense wrapper (the appositive case); the Degree atom at statement 6 inherits the same problem.

sentences: No one wants to work on Sundays.

issues: The habitual plural "on Sundays" is rendered as a single weekday slot (Time (sk_work $x) (Weekday sunday)) with no accompanying (Every (sk_work $x) 1 week), although the frequency rule says a named slot implies its cycle and mandates that companion atom — as emitted, the recurrence carried by the plural is lost.

sentences: Cattle are perfect food factories.

issues: (Inheritance cattle perfect) asserts that cattle are perfect simpliciter, whereas the sentence predicates perfection only relative to the food-factory role ('perfect AS food factories'), so splitting the adjective off the predicate nominal over-asserts.
The predication is metaphorical, and taken literally (with the genus atom) it derives that cattle are a subtype of factory, which the sentence does not claim.

sentences: Lake Towada is famous for its beauty.

issues: (For lake_towada sk_beauty_1) hangs the 'for'-complement on the entity instead of on the fame, so the parse never says what Lake Towada is famous FOR — the atom is disconnected from (Member lake_towada famous) and reads as a bare entity-to-entity relation.

sentences: The house requires large repairs.

issues: 'large' is a descriptive (size) modifier, which the Compound-concepts plural rule says must distribute over the members exactly like a copular predicate — i.e. an Implication over (PartOf $x sk_group_1) — but (Member sk_group_1 large) instead predicates largeness of the group-as-object, the form the instruction set explicitly warns against.

sentences: Dogs see everything in black and white.

issues: "in black and white" answers HOW dogs see, and the instruction set routes a PP answering where/when/how/whence/whither to the named role (here Manner), reserving the preposition-named oblique (In) for PPs that fit none of them.
